name: Slovak nationalism
summary: Slovak nationalism holds that Slovaks are a distinct nation entitled to their own language, culture and state, a cause that began in the 19th century against Magyarization and ended in independence in 1993. Today it is carried mainly by national-conservative and national-populist parties that stress sovereignty, traditional family and Christian values, restricted immigration, protection of the Slovak language and suspicion of minority autonomy, combined with a strong role for the state in the economy.
scope: The mainstream contemporary strand, as expressed by the Slovak National Party and, for social and sovereignty positions, Smer-SD under Fico, rooted in the Štúr-era revival and the 1848 Demands of the Slovak Nation. It does not model the wartime Hlinka's Slovak People's Party authoritarian state or the far-right fringe (for example Kotleba), and it treats the ethnic-versus-civic split as a point where adherents are divided. Sources are mostly encyclopedic and thin on written programme text, so many answers are inferred and marked low.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Smer-led governments kept state-funded health insurance and raised insurance contributions, and nationalist parties do not contest the post-socialist public health system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Smer's platform tied the minimum wage to 60% of the average wage, but the SNS opposed one proposed increase on budget grounds, so the nationalist camp is only mildly in favour.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The SNS backs economic nationalism and criticises privatisation, and Smer is described as etatist, so adherents distrust unfettered markets.

public-ownership.rationale: The SNS criticised privatisation and Smer's etatism favours state control of strategic sectors such as energy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Smer campaigned for a progressive income tax in place of the flat tax and raised minimum corporate taxes, which national-populists justify as fairness to ordinary Slovaks.

unions-good.rationale: Nationalist parties are not defined by a labour position; Smer is union-friendly while the SNS favours small business, so adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Smer defended the 13th pension and welfare for citizens while denouncing only perceived abuse by some Roma, so nationalists reject general welfare cuts.

strong-leader.rationale: Fico's style and the HSĽS leader cult show a strand favouring strong leaders, but mainstream nationalists work within parliamentary democracy.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: Smer backed tougher policing in Romani settlements and nationalists stress order and national defence.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

decide-locally.rationale: The SNS treated minority-rights and autonomy demands as steps to territorial separation and favours a unitary Slovak state.

traditional-family.rationale: The 2025 constitutional amendment backed by Smer and KDH defines mother and father by sex and restricts adoption to married heterosexual couples, and the SNS describes itself as based on Christian values.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The 2014 constitution defines marriage as one man and one woman, the 2025 amendment bans same-sex adoption, and the SNS proposed banning education on sexual orientation.

more-religion-public.rationale: The SNS cites Christian values as a pillar and Fico's government raised the threshold for registering churches, favouring established Christianity over newcomers.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The 2025 amendment recognises only two biologically defined sexes and the SNS wants gender-identity teaching banned, rejecting the social-construct claim.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving the Slovak language, culture and identity against Magyarization is the founding aim of Slovak nationalism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Fico said Islam has no place in Slovakia and Smer has an anti-immigration record, while the SNS shares the line.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.

reviewHistory.rationale: The SNS is Eurosceptic and the 2025 amendment asserts national law over EU law in cultural-ethical areas.

free-trade.rationale: The SNS favours domestic production but Slovakia is an export economy; the sources do not give a settled position.

nation-first.rationale: The SNS slogan is to serve the nation and Smer stresses national and state interests, and the 2025 amendment asserts national law.

open-borders.rationale: Parties that want reduced immigration and a Slovak nation-state do not aim at eventual open borders.

revolution-justified.rationale: Modern parliamentary nationalists work through elections, though the 1848 leaders did launch an armed rising.

central-planning.rationale: The SNS favours small business and domestic producers within a market system; planning is not a nationalist goal.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Smer's etatism and the SNS's economic nationalism both favour a state role in steering strategic industries.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nationalist parties govern a market economy and favour small business, so abolishing money and wages is foreign to the ideology.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nationalist parties accept state monetary institutions and none advocates abolishing the central bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The historical Slovak People's Party was corporatist, but modern mainstream nationalists do not advocate it; the strands split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Only the wartime HSĽS strand ran a one-party state; today's nationalist parties compete in elections.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1848 demands included universal suffrage and civic nationalism is the dominant view today, though populists criticise outcomes.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as a basis of power contradict a nation-state organised through parliament, as the SNS and Smer operate.

right-to-secede.rationale: The SNS read minority-autonomy demands as steps to secession and rejects them; the nation-state is defended as unitary, though Slovakia itself seceded from Czechoslovakia.

political-violence-never.rationale: The 1848 leaders launched an armed rebellion while modern nationalists operate peacefully, so adherents are split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The SNS invokes Christian values and Fico's government made registration harder for small religious groups, favouring a close state-church relation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian values are invoked in law, as in the constitutional marriage definition, but not scripture as the basis of law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Economic-nationalist etatism excludes privatising courts and defence.

military-superiority.rationale: The SNS accepts NATO but opposes a NATO base, and Slovakia is a small state, so the aim is defence rather than superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The page describes ethnic nationalism as influential and moderate and radical forms exist, though civic nationalism is now dominant, so adherents lean agree but are split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism treats nations and language as the units of history, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Nationalist programmes focus on national unity rather than outcome equality; Smer has social-democratic roots, so only mildly negative.

civilizational-union.rationale: Štúr moved toward pan-Slavism but modern Slovak nationalists mostly work within the EU framework; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nationalist sources describe no environmental philosophy; adherents could hold either an intrinsic or a use-based view.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalists want to sustain the nation's numbers and favour pronatalist family policy.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Neither the SNS nor Smer is documented on encryption; their security emphasis and populist distrust of the state point in opposite directions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Some strands (HSĽS) idealised a lost order, but the modern mainstream is not restorationist.

direct-action.rationale: Established nationalist parties work through elections and parliament.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources record no nationalist view on whether methods must mirror aims, so adherents' position is unknown.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A movement whose aim is a modern Slovak nation-state with its own language, schools and institutions cannot endorse a hunter-gatherer return.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The SNS promotes domestic production, agriculture and small business, all of which presuppose a division of labour.

production-for-use.rationale: Smer's etatism favours state economic roles but neither it nor the SNS frames production around use over profit, so this stays neutral.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The SNS favours small business and tax cuts for it; Marxist exploitation theory is not nationalist doctrine.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Nationalism rests on cross-class national community, so proletarian dictatorship over a former ruling class is rejected.

collective-farming.rationale: The SNS favours domestic agriculture; collectivisation is associated with the communist period that nationalism treats as imposed.

taxation-theft.rationale: Nationalist parties accept taxation to fund a state; Smer even raised taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: Nationalists restrict conduct on moral and national grounds, such as gender education bans.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The ideology claims collective rights for the nation, as in the 1848 demands for equality of nations.

conscription.rationale: Slovakia suspended conscription in 2006; nationalists do not stress it; split.

state-as-business.rationale: Smer's etatism treats the state as the father of citizens rather than as a business.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Some radicals' racial language about Roma exists, but this is not the mainstream position; the sources do not settle it.

organic-representation.rationale: The HSĽS tradition favoured corporatist representation, while modern parties work through parties.

total-state.rationale: Nationalists want a strong state but not totalitarian control; only the HSĽS radicals pursued a corporatist authoritarian state.

national-rebirth.rationale: The 19th-century revival used rebirth language, but the modern mainstream does not stress decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Slovak nationalists are defensive and fear Hungarian irredentism; no territorial claims abroad.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal-style loyalty is foreign to the modern nation-state ideology.

bound-labor.rationale: Štúr's 1848 programme sought an end to serfdom and return of land to peasants, so tying farmers to lords is rejected.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: SNS leader Danko called Israel a strategic partner and backed moving the embassy to Jerusalem.

revive-national-language.rationale: Štúr codified standard Slovak to replace Latin and Hungarian in public life, though today Slovak is not fallen out of use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The SNS favours small business owners and state-protected domestic firms, with no call for democratic worker or public votes in company governance.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Smer consolidated the budget but has favoured state spending; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: No nationalist source relies on rulers' moral example over law; Slovak parties legislate actively, as in the 2025 constitutional changes.

national-self-determination.rationale: Slovak nationalism is built on the nation's right to its own language and state, from the 1848 demands to independence in 1993.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nationalist parties invoke Christian values and reject exclusive rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Fico attacks welfare abuse and nationalists favour reserving benefits for citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Fico described Roma as welfare abusers and backed stricter conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rejection of class struggle and the Catholic social-teaching roots of Slovak nationalism favour cooperation of classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Matica slovenská and Slovak schools were closed under Hungary in 1874-75, making preservation of inherited cultural institutions central.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism holds that working people belong within national lines, not an international class.

ban-interest.rationale: Nationalist programmes support market banking; no call to ban interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The 1848 demands sought equal rights, and no mainstream Slovak party advocates racial segregation, though SNS figures made racist remarks about Roma.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Nationalists see the state as the nation's instrument, not a class tool.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Anti-immigration nationalists expect integration into Slovak culture, though sources give no explicit demand.

elite-replacement.rationale: Some radicals (Kotleba) promote it but mainstream parties do not.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Conservative family stance rejects the structural-patriarchy thesis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about elites being out of touch or general anti-establishment feeling, not about elites putting their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

reviewHistory.rationale: National-populism frames elites as out of touch, a stock Smer and SNS theme.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of mainstream programmes and contradicts Christian values.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Smer's etatism and the SNS economic nationalism assign the state a broad economic and social role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Radical wing statements on Roma exist but the mainstream does not endorse it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Civic nationalism accepts equal rights while ethnic strands put Slovaks first, so tension.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Fico restricted new church registration but conversion itself is not restricted.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian-values stance favours religious instruction in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The statement concerns a socialist state theory that Slovak nationalists do not hold; their view of the state is national, not socialist.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1848 demands sought universal suffrage and civic nationalism accepts popular consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Radicals including the HSĽS wanted to remove Czechs and Hungarians, but the mainstream no longer does; adherents split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Slovak nationalism defends the nation's survival against stronger neighbours but sources do not frame struggle as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Slovak governments have moved to dissolve Kotleba's party, but nationalist position not sourced.

separated-powers.rationale: Slovakia has a constitutional separation of powers which parties accept; though Fico's governments have pressed against judiciary.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nationalism organises the nation across classes through ordinary parties like the SNS, so a vanguard party leading the working class is rejected.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Christian social teaching favours the poor but nationalists prioritise citizens.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Smer has historic union ties while the SNS favours small business, so adherents are split and sources record no firm position.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ethnic nationalists see Hungarian and Roma presence as a threat to cohesion, though civic nationalists dissent.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The 1848 demands sought elected representation and equal suffrage, and Slovak nationalist parties contest elections for office.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Sources record no nationalist position; security emphasis pulls toward yes while attachment to constitutional order pulls toward no.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Smer introduced price controls on food items and caps on energy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Smer-led governments have changed public broadcasting while formally defending media pluralism.

party-commands-army.rationale: Slovakia's constitution subordinates the army to the state, and nationalist parties operating within it do not seek party control.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Populist rhetoric against elites could support it, but the sources record no such demand from nationalist parties.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: SNS is Eurosceptic and the 2025 amendment asserts Slovak law over EU law in some domains.

clerical-rule.rationale: Slovak nationalism claims popular and national sovereignty, and even the Catholic HSĽS left rule to the party rather than to senior clergy as such.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Loyalty to the nation is the movement's core, so working for one's own government's defeat is the opposite of the nationalist stance.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Sources do not document nationalist views on presidential term limits.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The SNS accepts NATO, while opposing NATO bases, so rejects ending alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Forced home ownership has no place in any nationalist programme and is inconsistent with property-friendly economic nationalism.

people-in-arms.rationale: Štúr-era demands included a Slovak national guard, but modern nationalists accept a professional army.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Slovaks are not divided between states in a way they claim reunification of.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist rhetoric by Fico targets elites, media and NGOs; the sources do not specifically address university-educated people.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The SNS has advocated banning gender-identity and sexual-orientation education and the 2025 amendment strengthens parental control of curricula.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Ethnic strand of Slovak nationalism identifies the nation by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: The SNS sought limits on Hungarian-language use and saw minority rights as a step toward autonomy.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Fico's government raised the registration threshold for churches.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Economic nationalists call for domestic ownership to make independence real.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The 1848 demands emphasised press and assembly freedoms and nationalists do not claim development justifies suppressing them.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Slovakia is a small NATO member whose nationalists accept NATO but oppose a NATO base, with no call for national nuclear arms.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Slovakia directly elects its president since 1999 and nationalists accept it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Catholic social teaching and Smer's etatism support limits on property.

precautionary-principle.rationale: No nationalist source addresses environmental precaution, so this is neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: The SNS accepts NATO membership although it opposes a NATO base, so it endorses the alliance's mutual-defence principle.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Smer and the SNS favour the established Christian churches, and Fico's law raised the registration threshold for religious bodies.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Slovak presidents are directly elected and often partisan-linked; sources show no nationalist doctrine on neutrality.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Slovak nationalism is a modern national movement without a sacred ruler, and Slovakia is a republic.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Smer campaigned to replace the flat tax with a progressive income tax, and nationalist populists defend progressive burden-sharing.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nationalists stress inherited national character but also upbringing in national culture, and sources do not settle the question.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The 1848 demands sought constitutional guarantees and Slovakia's constitution binds rulers to law, so a ruler above the law is rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: The sources link neither the SNS nor Smer to space policy, so adherents' view on a civilisational space goal is unknown.

leader-cult.rationale: HSĽS had a leader cult around Hlinka; modern parties do not.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis foreign to nationalism, which treats the nation as the unit of politics and rejects class struggle.

land-redistribution.rationale: 1848 demands returned land to peasants but modern programmes do not.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Slovaks fear Hungary making precisely such claims; the SNS opposes Hungarian Status Law.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: A modern Slovak republic with constitutional freedoms and Christian-values parties does not seek legal penalties for leaving a religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Fico said Islam has no place in Slovakia, but nationalists seek to exclude Islamic practice rather than impose covering.

common-currency.rationale: Slovakia adopted the euro; Smer accepts it while SNS is critical; split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Štúr moved toward pan-Slavism but modern nationalists do not push union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The SNS viewed broader minority rights as a step toward territorial autonomy, so it resists self-governing minority institutions.

ban-cartels.rationale: The SNS favours small business but sources do not document a competition-law position.

no-bailouts.rationale: Smer's etatist government cushioned the economy, while the SNS opposed spending; sources record no position on bailouts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The 2025 constitutional amendment backed by Smer reaffirms two sexes and traditional roles, and quotas are not part of nationalist programmes.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Economic nationalism supports domestic production but not closed blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Sources do not document nationalist views on binding trade standards; labour protection and anti-supranationalism conflict.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Established nationalist parties compete in parliament; foco insurgency is the opposite of their method.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The 1848 demands called for equal civil rights and returning land taken by the aristocracy; modern nationalists accept a republic.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Slovak nationalism rests on a claimed historical state right tied to Great Moravia, so national-centred history is core.

patriotic-education.rationale: Cultivating national identity and loyalty is the point of the movement, and the SNS slogan stresses serving the nation.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Slovakia never ruled an empire, and its nationalists focus on defending their own nation rather than regaining influence abroad.

delink-world-market.rationale: Slovak nationalists support domestic production but not delinking from world trade, since Slovakia is an export economy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis nationalists do not engage; they emphasise national solidarity across classes.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Economic nationalists favour state intervention and the SNS opposes minority privileges; a libertarian right to discriminate is not part of their view.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Slovakia has an entrenched constitution that nationalist parties used to amend marriage and sex provisions, but the sources show no principled view on bills of rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: Slovakia is a republic with directly elected president and nationalists operate within it; hereditary rule is not part of the ideology.

minority-veto.rationale: The SNS rejects minority claims to special rights against a national majority.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 1848 demands sought representation and Slovakia is a parliamentary republic, though the national-law-over-EU stance limits supranational rather than parliamentary power.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nationalism is a political movement demanding active national participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The sources contain no nationalist view on mass culture; Fico attacks media as hostile, which does not settle the question.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not a documented nationalist thesis, though economic nationalists resent foreign ownership.

native-born-offices.rationale: The sources show no demand, though ethnic nationalists could accept it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Economic nationalism favours domestic production but Slovakia accepts EU funds.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Slovakia lost no territory it seeks to reclaim; Hungarian revisionism is the threat nationalists fear.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Smer invokes the anti-fascist Slovak National Uprising but the SNS rehabilitates Tiso, so adherents split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-communist and Tiso-sympathising strands disagree, so split.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The SNS honoured Tiso with a plaque in Žilina, indicating preference for keeping national memorials even when contested.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Slovakia has civilian control of the army and no nationalist party seeks otherwise.

paid-care-work.rationale: Smer favours family support but sources do not record support for paying domestic care as labour.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism favours blocking foreign purchase of strategic firms.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Smer defended the public pension pillar and 13th pension against private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The SNS defends domestic ownership and agriculture, and the 1848 demands sought return of land to peasant owners, not communal tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Slovakia's constitution requires this and nationalists accept it.

single-official-language.rationale: Slovak as the state language is central, from Štúr's codification to language protection laws, though minority use is tolerated in practice.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Economic nationalism and Slovak sensitivity about foreign purchase favour restrictions on land ownership.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale does not support its value under the reworded statement: it documents disclosure, not restriction.

reviewHistory.rationale: The SNS proposed scrutiny of foreign-funded NGOs on the Hungarian model, and Smer's 2025 amendment requires donor disclosure (s2, s4). These measures screen funding; the sources do not describe outright restriction.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale does not support its value under the reworded statement: it documents disclosure, not restriction.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Nationalists favour pro-family policy over immigration to maintain population.

residents-only-property.rationale: Nationalists favour limiting foreign land ownership but sources do not document local residency limits.

non-intervention.rationale: Smer defends non-interference in other countries and the sovereignty of states.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The HSĽS radical wing spread such conspiracies, but mainstream nationalists dispute; split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The constitution defines marriage as one man and one woman and nationalists defend this, so abolishing legal marriage is rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The SNS proposed charging media for information requests, while Smer's NGO law extends information rules, so adherents are split.

local-production.rationale: The SNS backs economic nationalism, domestic production and agriculture, matching buying and producing locally.

informal-organisation.rationale: Slovak nationalists organise through registered parties like the SNS and Smer, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The 2025 amendment declares Slovak law takes precedence over EU law in cultural and ethical matters.

religious-nation.rationale: Slovak identity is tied to Catholic and Lutheran traditions but defined chiefly by language, so split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Slovak nationalism arose against domination by a dominant neighbour.

defeat-communism.rationale: Smer shows communist nostalgia while SNS anti-communist, split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Smer favours a public role while the SNS favours small business; sources record no position on service delivery mixes.

religion-illusion.rationale: The SNS describes itself as based on Christian values, so the claim that religion is a consoling illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Neither the SNS nor Smer frames capitalism as a historical stage; adherents are mixed on its record.

treaties-binding.rationale: The statement concerns indigenous treaties, which have no analogue in Slovak nationalist politics.

cooperative-communities.rationale: A nation-state movement with a national economy has no place for property-sharing small communities as a model.

majority-settlement.rationale: The HSĽS radicals wanted minorities removed, but modern mainstream nationalists do not document settlement policies; adherents split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Slovak nationalism rested on a historical state right tied to Great Moravia.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The wartime Slovak State deported Jews and parts of the movement praise Tiso, but Holocaust denial is not mainstream nationalist doctrine.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Nationalists oppose same-sex marriage and adoption but not criminalisation, which Slovakia abolished.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Mainstream nationalist parties like the SNS and Smer compete in elections and defend their own right to oppose.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The SNS invokes Christian values, but modern Slovakia has no such law and sources record no call to create one.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Slovakia has no colonies and its nationalism arose in opposition to domination, so rule for the benefit of the metropole is rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A statement of Islamic doctrine; Slovak nationalists reject Islam's place in Slovakia and would not endorse the duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A statement of Islamist doctrine that Slovak nationalists, who say Islam has no place in Slovakia, reject.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The SNS and Smer oppose gender-identity education and anti-discrimination frameworks, so intersectional analysis is rejected.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The 2025 amendment recognises only two biologically defined sexes and the SNS has sought to ban gender-identity teaching.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Fico said in 2016 that Islam has no place in Slovakia and the party record is anti-immigration, though this is one leader's statement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Catholic HSĽS tradition accepted divine authority while the 1848 liberal-democratic strand grounded authority in the people, so adherents split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Fico's anti-Islam stance may favour limits, but sources record no position on religious dress in institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The audited sources record no nationalist position on nondisclosure agreements or arbitration in harassment cases.

social-market-economy.rationale: Smer combines market economy with social protection like the 13th pension, though the SNS leans toward economic nationalism.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Smer wants less alignment with the West but retains NATO; split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Slovakia is a republic with a directly elected president, and no Slovak nationalist party seeks hereditary rule.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Smer imposed its own fiscal consolidation, but its rhetoric opposes foreign dictates, so adherents split.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1848 demands sought universal male suffrage, and modern nationalists accept universal suffrage.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Fico attacks media as hostile, but sources do not record a wealth-based critique.

racial-franchise.rationale: Slovak nationalism claims civic equality at least formally, and the 1848 demands sought universal suffrage.

open-government-data.rationale: Smer's NGO law extends freedom-of-information rules, but no position on open publication is documented.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The SNS bases itself on Christian values, so it opposes state atheism, a feature of the communist period.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Smer backed tougher policing and nationalists emphasise order, so abolition is rejected.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 2025 amendment defines father and mother by sex but sources do not describe marital authority.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The HSĽS had paramilitary and youth organisations, but modern mainstream nationalists do not; the strands split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The SNS accepts NATO membership but opposes a NATO base or logistics centre on Slovak territory.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nationalists defend armed national defence, and the Christian tradition they invoke accepts self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Slovak nationalism rests on a historical state right traced to the Great Moravian Empire, claiming continuity of identity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The 2025 constitutional amendment defines two sexes biologically, which Smer and its partners adopted.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: SNS figures honoured Tiso, executed in 1947, as a Slovak son, showing a tendency to honour those who died for the national cause.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The HSĽS framed politics against Marxist and liberal enemies in religious terms, but modern parties do not.

culture-before-state.rationale: Štúr's circle codified the Slovak language and built cultural institutions before the 1848 political demands, which sets the movement's sequence.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The SNS backs economic nationalism and domestic ownership, and its leaders have targeted minorities, so adherents favour Slovak majority control.

independent-unions.rationale: Smer has had close relations with unions; the sources do not document positions on union independence.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Smer's etatism and the SNS critique of privatisation favour keeping utilities and hospitals in public hands.

second-chamber.rationale: Slovakia has a unicameral National Council and nationalist parties have not asked for a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Nationalists favour national ownership or private domestic ownership, not municipal ownership.

family-wage.rationale: The Catholic social teaching in the HSĽS tradition (Rerum novarum) endorses a family wage; modern parties echo it in family policy.

person-over-state.rationale: Nationalism ranks the national community alongside or above the individual; the SNS describes itself as serving the nation.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Christian-values parties like the SNS and the Catholic HSĽS accept a spiritual dimension of human nature.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Defenders of a unitary Slovak state would keep regional self-government dependent on the National Council.

racial-pride.rationale: Slovak nationalism stresses ethnic and national pride rather than race; adherents' view on racial pride is unclear.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Slovak nationalism arose defensively, and the SNS accepts NATO as a defensive alliance.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Štúr codified a Slovak standard to unite dialect speakers as one nation, but modern nationalists also stress state right and history.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The SNS's main concern after 1993 was Hungarian irredentism, treating minority rights as steps to partition.

free-public-college.rationale: Slovakia already has tuition-free public universities and no nationalist party has proposed ending it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: No audited source records a nationalist claim about distinct women's values in public life.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

capital-controls.rationale: Economic nationalists might favour them but sources do not document the position.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A nation-state movement accepts the state's monopoly on armed force; Slovak law already provides this.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Loyalty to the nation in war is a core nationalist value.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Smer is union-friendly but the SNS is not; sources record no firm position.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Smer favours social support but sources do not record a position on in-work tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Smer defends flexible spending while consolidating, and sources record no principled stance.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Slovak nationalists have not been documented as calling for reform of international economic rules for developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Nationalist parties aim to run the state, not smash it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: A unitary nationalist state favours one national economic system.

sacred-nation.rationale: The movement treats the nation as a community of lasting significance tied to historical state right.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Christian-conservative nationalists accept an unchanging human nature grounding dignity.

public-service-media.rationale: Smer-led governments reshaped the public broadcaster, so adherents' position on independence is contested.

workers-own-party.rationale: Nationalists organise across classes and reject separate class parties.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Slovak law grants equal inheritance and nationalists have not contested it.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The sources give no nationalist view on trading liberty for environmental protection.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The Slovak language is the core marker of the nation since Štúr, and anti-immigration parties would expect immigrants to learn it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Smer has union ties while the SNS favours employers, so adherents are split and sources record no position.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1848 demands sought universal suffrage and Slovak nationalists today do not question women's vote.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: SNS opposes autonomy for the Hungarian minority and is suspicious of minority territorial claims.

simple-living.rationale: Nationalist parties promote small business and traditional values but are not committed to self-sufficient living.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The nationalist revival from Štúr to the SNS rests on the Slovak nation's attachment to and duty to defend its land and heritage.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Mainstream Slovak nationalism operates within the constitution and rule of law, and the strand modelled excludes the authoritarian wartime state.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Slovak nationalism supports Slovaks abroad and Slovak-language protection, though active state support for kin minorities is less documented.

national-resource-control.rationale: The strand stresses sovereignty and a strong state role in the economy, so national control over resources is a natural expression of it.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Smer and SNS combine national sovereignty with state protection of workers and social benefits, documented in their etatist platforms.

police-more-powers.rationale: Smer backed tougher policing in Romani settlements and nationalists stress order and national defence. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Smer defended the 13th pension and welfare for citizens while denouncing only perceived abuse by some Roma, so nationalists reject general welfare cuts. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

notes: Adherents split between an ethnic strand (Slota-era SNS, wartime Slovak People's Party) and a civic strand now described as dominant. Smer is included for sovereignty and family positions although its economics is social-democratic. Hlinka's Wikipedia page was not opened; his figure rests on the Slovak People's Party page.
